clue.text: Father munched a pet slug, say

indicators.note: something munched is taken into the mouth, so the first piece swallows the second

parts.note: God the Father
a pet is a fit of sulking, as is a strop

explanation.surface: Dad chewing up a slug that someone kept as a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' is the old sense 'in a pet', a sulk, rather than an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is an example of a gastropod, the mollusc class that also includes snails; 'say' flags the example.

clue.text: Some wind, as leg cocked up

indicators.note: cocked up is slang for botched, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A dog lifting its leg and breaking wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocked up' pictures a dog's raised leg but means bungled, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gales are strong blasts of moving air, hence a quantity of wind.

clue.text: Important guarantee saving time

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe within, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: a seal is a mark that guarantees authenticity
MIN is short for minute, a unit of time

explanation.surface: A key warranty that preserves your time.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminal work is highly influential, shaping what follows it, so of great importance.

clue.text: Arm a little longer, if leg!

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wishing an arm were slightly longer, if only it were a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are weapons, and a rifle is one such firearm.

clue.text: Racket — schpyreme?

parts.note: this made-up word is a familiar word for a plot with three extra letters set in its middle; read the instruction that would build it

explanation.surface: A bare nonsense word set against a word for a swindle, as though naming one.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: put PYR amid SCHEME and you get SCH-PYR-EME, the clue's odd word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyramid scheme is a fraudulent racket paying early investors with later recruits' money.

clue.text: Embarrassment initially hidden by god after dropping trousers

indicators.note: after places the god part behind the dropping part in the answer

parts.note: a dropping is animal dung

indicators.note: hidden by means held inside the next piece, the god's name

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone red-faced after their trousers fall down in front of a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping trousers' reads as a pratfall, but 'dropping' is DUNG and 'trousers' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are hard-wearing work trousers, often with a bib, so a kind of trousers.

clue.text: Royal staff sprayed tear gas

definitions.meaning: the ceremonial staff carried before a monarch or speaker

explanation.surface: Palace servants were hit with tear gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is both a ceremonial rod of office and a chemical irritant spray.

clue.text: See 22 across
Arena where Greek character served up after death in old athlete

indicators.note: after places the Greek letter behind the rest
in places the death word inside the athlete's name

parts.note: Seb Coe, the British Olympic middle-distance runner of the 1980s
a death is a loss

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters are written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A stadium where a Greek figure was served up after a former athlete died.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum in Rome is the most famous ancient amphitheatre, the arena of gladiators.

clue.text: Choose suspect Prof, suspect Prof

parts.note: Professor Plum is a suspect in Cluedo, the British murder-mystery board game known as Clue in America

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: Pick the shady academic, that shady academic.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase is used two ways: first as a Cluedo character, then as an anagram of PROF.
explanation.definitionFit: To plump for is an idiom meaning to decide on or opt for one thing.

clue.text: Score reduced, see, in a good way

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to score is to nick, cut a notch
Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in England

explanation.surface: A lowered score, you see, is good.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicely is the adverb of nice, describing something done well or pleasantly.

clue.text: Doctor can use time allocated for payment

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: A physician may take the time set aside for settling a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Usance is the period allowed by custom for paying a foreign bill of exchange.

clue.text: Most substantial estimate needing revision

indicators.note: needing revision says the letters must be reworked

explanation.surface: The biggest quote had to be revised.
explanation.definitionFit: Meatiest means having the most meat, figuratively most solid or weighty in content.

clue.text: See 24
Superior novel about victory claimed by winner

indicators.note: claimed by means taken into the winner's possession, so placed inside

parts.note: an ace is a winning serve in tennis

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A first-rate novel about a triumph, won by a champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut above is an idiom meaning noticeably better than the rest.

clue.text: Blundering in a ledger straightened out again

indicators.note: blundering means making mistakes, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An accounting error was corrected a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to bring back into line, so straightened once more.

clue.text: Hang around back of barge on river that's dredged

indicators.note: on places the river before the rest as written in the answer

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: around means the hanging word surrounds the next letter

parts.note: to pend is to hang, be undecided

indicators.note: back of takes the last letter of the barge word

explanation.surface: Loiter at the stern of a barge on a river that has been dredged.
explanation.definitionFit: Dredging a channel removes silt, which makes the water deeper.

clue.text: Better off study group

parts.note: off means out, as in a light that is off or out
a class is a group of students

explanation.surface: Superior students have left the study group.
explanation.definitionFit: To outclass is to surpass by a wide margin, as 'better' does as a verb.

clue.text: Cold person inflicting pain? Sweet talker

parts.note: C stands for cold on taps
a harmer is one who harms

explanation.surface: An icy sadist turns out to be a smooth flatterer.
explanation.definitionFit: A charmer wins people over with pleasing words, so a smooth-tongued flatterer.

clue.text: Bandage parts?

parts.note: the word parts is the word strap written upwards, as it would be in a down light

explanation.surface: Body parts that need wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: STRAP, written upwards in this down light, gives PARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To strap up a wound or joint is to bind it with bandaging.

clue.text: See 4
A Romeo encapsulated by his allure, spicy stuff

indicators.note: encapsulated by means enclosed within the following words

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
SA is sex appeal, i.e. allure

explanation.surface: A lover wrapped up in his own charm, a hot property.
explanation.definitionFit: Harissa is a hot North African chilli paste, a fiery condiment.

clue.text: Gallant boxer punching person going down?

indicators.note: punching means driving into, so the boxer goes inside

parts.note: a caver descends into caves
Muhammad Ali, the boxer

explanation.surface: A brave fighter hitting someone being knocked to the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going down' suggests a knockdown, but means a potholer's descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cavalier was a dashing Royalist horseman; a gallant is a dashing gentleman of fashion.

clue.text: War hero's conception: vital force interrupting broadcasting of German unit

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the other piece
broadcasting means scattering widely, so these letters are spread around

parts.note: chi is the life force in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: A wartime hero's idea, where energy cuts into a German army unit's radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasting' suggests radio but is the anagram of GERMAN UNIT, giving TURING MAN E, which CHI interrupts.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Turing, the Bletchley Park codebreaker, conceived the theoretical computing device named after him.

clue.text: Chinese dynasty ending in Rosario — steps taken here?

parts.note: the Tang dynasty ruled China 618 to 907

indicators.note: ending in takes the last letter of the city's name

explanation.surface: A Chinese dynasty ending up in an Argentine city, where dance steps are taken.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosario is in Argentina, home of the dance, so the definition reads as the whole surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance, a set of steps performed together.

clue.text: Poor man, wage slave earned money, finally

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A wage slave earned money at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy means lacking the necessities of life, hence impoverished.

clue.text: Author, one hammering home the teachings of Joseph Smith, Spoonerised?

indicators.note: Spoonerised says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped, after Rev Spooner

parts.note: Joseph Smith founded Mormonism
a nailer hammers in nails

explanation.surface: A writer pressing home a church's doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of MORMON NAILER gives NORMAN MAILER; the swap is by sound since MORMON becomes NORMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman Mailer was an American novelist, author of The Naked and the Dead.

clue.text: Under pressure with National Insurance contribution, made to pay

indicators.note: a contribution is something put in, so the abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: being pushed is being under pressure
NI is National Insurance, the British social-security tax

explanation.surface: Pressed for the payroll tax, made to cough up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being punished is being made to suffer for wrongdoing, as in paying the penalty.

clue.text: Too much honey?

definitions.meaning: honey and ... are both terms of endearment

explanation.surface: Is honey overpriced, or too sweet?
explanation.definitionFit: Dear means both high-priced and a loved one addressed fondly.

clue.text: Decline honour in delicate art of discretion

parts.note: a dip is a decline or fall

indicators.note: in places the honour inside the delicate word

parts.note: lacy means delicate, like lace
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Turning down a medal in the subtle art of tact.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomacy is skill in handling affairs tactfully, without giving offence.
